Looking for motivated teammates interested in coding, AI, data analysis, design, and lunar exploration. Let’s build something great!
summary: LUNAR NAV is an interactive web-based tool for planning and comparing potential lunar landing sites, with a focus on the Moon’s south pole. It allows users to explore the lunar surface in 3D, select locations and dates, and visualize the position of the Sun and Earth relative to the local horizon. The platform helps evaluate sunlight availability for power generation and identify potential direct-to-Earth communication windows. Users can compare different landing sites and time periods to better understand their advantages and limitations. By bringing complex lunar observation data and mission-planning concepts into an intuitive visual interface, LUNAR NAV makes lunar exploration planning more accessible to researchers, educators, and the public. It aims to support better-informed decisions for future lunar missions.
details:
LUNAR NAV is a web application designed to make planning future lunar missions easier, especially missions to the Moon’s south pole. The project combines an interactive 3D model of the Moon with tools for exploring potential landing locations and understanding the conditions that astronauts and equipment may face on the lunar surface.

Users can explore the Moon, select possible landing sites and examine the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the lunar horizon. This is important because sunlight affects how much energy a solar-powered lunar base or rover could receive, while the position of Earth determines potential opportunities for direct communication with our planet. Comparing different locations and dates can help users understand why choosing a landing site is not as simple as finding a flat area.

I wanted to create something more interactive than a page full of scientific numbers and charts. Instead, LUNAR NAV presents lunar exploration in a visual and accessible way, allowing users to explore the environment and connect astronomical information with real mission challenges.

The application was developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with web-based 3D visualization technologies. AI-assisted development tools were also used during the development process. The project is deployed on Vercel and can be accessed directly through a web browser.

The main idea behind LUNAR NAV is to make complex lunar mission-planning concepts easier to understand and explore. It could be useful for students, educators and anyone interested in space exploration. In the future, I would like to expand it with more precise lunar terrain data, improved calculations and additional tools for comparing landing sites.

While developing the project, I focused on scientific relevance, usability, visual clarity and the specific challenges of the lunar south pole, particularly extreme lighting conditions and communication with Earth.
